title: Zach Bryan’s ‘Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs’ Debuts Atop Three Album Charts
summary: Plus, all eight of its tracks enter Hot Country Songs and Hot Rock Songs.
contentText:
Zach Bryan ’s Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs debuts at No. 1 on Billboard ’s Top Country Albums, Top Rock Albums and Americana/Folk Albums charts, and No. 2 on the Billboard 200, earning 65,000 equivalent album units in the United States in its first week, Oct. 16-22, according to Luminate.

The set is Bryan’s fifth to top those three tallies. It follows January’s With Heaven on Top , 2024’s The Great American Bar Scene , 2023’s self-titled release and 2022’s American Heartbreak . With Heaven on Top and Zach Bryan also led the all-genre Billboard 200.

Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs likewise makes an immediate splash at the song level. All eight of its tracks debut on Hot Country Songs and Hot Rock Songs, led by the Lana Del Rey-featuring “Lies,” which enters at No. 1 on the latter, becoming their fourth and first leader, respectively, and No. 2 on the former. The haul swells one of the deepest catalogs in the style, as Bryan has now charted 106 titles on Hot Rock Songs and 97 on Hot Country Songs.

Few artists open in the Hot Country Songs top 10 like Bryan. With “Lies” and “Lodi When” bowing at Nos. 2 and 9, he has now debuted 14 of his 17 career top 10s directly in the tier. That’s the third-most top 10 debuts among all acts since the chart adopted its multimetric methodology in October 2012, trailing only Morgan Wallen (34) and Taylor Swift (17). Bryan’s two No. 1s are “Something in the Orange” and his Kacey Musgraves collaboration “I Remember Everything,” which ruled for six and 20 weeks, respectively.

On the Billboard Hot 100, “Lies” enters at No. 4, becoming Bryan’s fourth top 10 and Del Rey’s third.

The streaming numbers also put Bryan’s reach in perspective. During the tracking week, he ranked fourth among all artists in the U.S., drawing 151.3 million official streams. He trailed only Drake (298.6 million), Wallen (204.2 million) and Swift (183.1 million).
